quest.title: Legendary "Color"
quest.description: You accept the Chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind's commission, and are determined to complete the task that you have been entrusted with...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x375, Mora x34075, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act II
chapter.title: Legendary "Color"

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Look at this view. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's gorgeous!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Now, try looking a little further.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... That graffiti...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: In all the years since the founding of our tribe, those colors have been with us every step of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It is true that I seek to bring new life to this ancient tribe through change and reform. But I also understand there are certain foundational things that we cannot afford to throw away.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The foremost of these is the way we record our history.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Since the very beginnings, our tribe has always sought to bring color to history, and I have a deep sense that this is one part of our heritage that we should not give up.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: So whatever it takes, I must find a way for us to continue producing our traditional woven scrolls.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're completely right. Paimon's sorry for what she said earlier. It was out of line...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It's quite alright. I'm just grateful you're able to understand where I'm coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're committed to helping you solve this.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Then let us hope that when we next meet, we succeed in reviving this tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: I take it you're the ones appointed by Elder Tlapo?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! And you are?

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Call me Toltec. The chief asked me to be your guide for the day. His messengers already filled me in on the situation. So just follow me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haven't we been in here before, though?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, but don't forget we're the chosen ones.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: The strange thing is, our ancestors never removed the seal even after they finished the graffiti art.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Since it was sealed off, the only person who's been inside is the great shaman, Huitzilin. And that was two hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: According to her, the artwork tells the story of a hero by the name of Kuntur...

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: ...But I digress. Sorry, I'm a big fan of graffiti artwork, once I get talking I can go on for hours.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you're sure you don't wanna come with us?

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: I'll pass. I tried to get in once, but the seal blocked my way. I tried getting my Iktomisaurus to clear it with its powers, but even that didn't work.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: I guess it's supposed to be a test left there by our ancestors. If you don't pass the test, you're not worthy of viewing their works of art.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw...

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Don't worry about me though. I wouldn't be joining you this time, even if I was able to get in.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Unlike our chief, I don't have the guts to challenge our traditions. This task is specifically appointed to someone by the Iktomisaur Elder. Who knows what bad things might happen if I got involved?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fair enough. Alright, we'll try not to take too long!

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: You two head on in. I'll wait right here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place! That fruit Toltec mentioned should be the one on the wall, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't notice it last time we were here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now the only question is, which ones do we pick?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is probably where my special ability the chief mentioned comes in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, go ahead, try it out!

talks.objective: Try using the Iktomisaur's special Elemental Sight

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These guys' ancestors made some real works of art here. But based on what we've seen so far, it seems like there should be more to the story.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you think maybe there's more artwork further inside? Seems kinda strange...

choices.text: We can go take a look if you want?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, no need — Paimon was just thinking aloud. Toltec's waiting for us, and we have a job to do, so maybe it's best if we head out now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's head back and meet up with Toltec!

choices.text: Maybe — but we have a job to do. We should focus on that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, you're right. There's always next time.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Take a look at this — it's a woven scroll made by one of our ancestors. This is the kind of thing we're trying to make.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The person depicted is the legendary shaman, Huitzilin. She lived two hundred years ago, and was once appointed by the Iktomisaur Elder like yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: She was especially skilled in the art of color manipulation, and of course completed her task with flying colors.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: This scroll is a record of her deeds, and was most likely the work of her own hand. The quality is simply breathtaking, even compared to other scrolls of this variety.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Sadly, since she passed away, all of our Iktomisaur Elder's subsequent appointees have had to rely on the "gift from the spirits" to complete their work.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But now, you're about to revive an older tradition.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: That's a good way of putting it. My only quibble with your phrasing would be, it's not just me, but "us."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Now Paimon's getting excited.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Bring out the samples.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: An assistant presents the samples for test-dyeing.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Now, as I mentioned, the dyeing process is a little complicated, but I am confident you will manage. Just make sure to follow my instructions carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Will do. Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: The pattern has already been sketched out on the sample, so you just need to dye each block with the correct color. But you'll need to wait for the dye to fully soak in between each step to make sure the colors don't run.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Dye the fabric as instructed.)

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Good. The dye has taken to the fabric, and the pattern is crisp and clear. Next, apply all the remaining dye and we should see that elusive signature color emerge.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, final step!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Apply the remaining dye.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Did it work? Paimon doesn't see it...

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: That color isn't showing up... The dyeing has failed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did I mess up somehow?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: No, your technique was flawless. You did everything exactly as instructed. It would have made no difference if I'd done it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then what went wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: It could be the weaving technique, or maybe the dye has to be applied in a different way... Whatever the case, it looks like I have failed to get to the bottom of this mystery.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry... Paimon wishes we could do more to help.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I am the one who should be apologizing. I made you do so much work, and it was for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I will of course honor my commitment to compensate you for your trouble, but I do hope you won't give up on this task. I plan to keep investigating, and will be sure to keep you updated with any progress.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we're not quitters!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon does have a question though... Um, this whole process of recording history on woven scrolls seems so complicated. Why don't you just write it down instead?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You said yourself, you're all about change and reform. Well, this seems like a pretty good place to start, don't you think? Writing things down would be easier for everyone, and your records would be more detailed.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: ...I think you've perhaps misunderstood my philosophy, but that's okay. I can answer your question, but there's somewhere I need to show you first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... sure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Remember the last time we came here? We found all of the artwork throughout the cave. These guys' ancestors created a real masterpiece!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They probably used the same stuff for their paint as we're using for the dye, right? Maybe we'll create a masterpiece of our own!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Then we'd better get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, let's head back and meet up with Toltec!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're back! And we found the ingredients for the dye.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Sounds like you made it through the seal then! Our Iktomisaur Elder was right about you.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: It's getting late. Follow me, I'll take us back.

talks.objective: Return to the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Toltec has updated me on your progress. Well done, I appreciate your efforts.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing! Here's the stuff for the dye.

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: I see... yes, this is certainly a very different substance from typical dyes... Okay, now let's try our hand at making some samples. The fabric is ready for testing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it!

dialogues.speaker: Biram
dialogues.text: Please, follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the dye is somewhere in this cave, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: This is as far as I can take you. Only the appointed ones may proceed from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why's that?

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Kind of a long story. Apparently, there's a certain fruit that grows in this cave, the juice of which can be processed to make an excellent dye.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: Many years ago, our ancestors set out to make a series of ambitious works of graffiti art. They selected this cave to make them in, presumably due to the availability of the dye.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: However, they didn't want anyone to see their work before it was completed. And so, they sealed off the entrance to control access.

dialogues.speaker: Toltec
dialogues.text: To bypass the seal, you have to have mastered the art of color perception, or something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like there's no way past... Maybe try the same thing as before?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You saw something, right? Whatever it was, grab it!
